If you're like me you look in the mirror on occasion and wish your arms were just an inch or so bigger. Or maybe you're satisfied with them when they're pumped, but think they look like floppy broomsticks otherwise.

Well, the one of easiest ways to grow any bodypart is to start putting it through it's full range of motion if you aren't already doing so. This applies especially to triceps, and even more especially to triceps on bodyweight athletes, since if you're on the standard diet of pushups, handstand pushups and dips for your pushing chain, you're missing out on a good part of the later half of the movement. This is most people who do bodyweight fitness.

Of course, you can do some awkward bodyweight triceps extensions on rings or straps if you have them, or you can just "cheat" and use dumbbells. But you might not have either of those things around. And regardless, I think I've found a better way. I've started doing this recently and my triceps do seem to be responding.

My solution is elbows-to-ground pushups. These are great because you can do them anywhere, with no equipment, and it puts your triceps through their full range of motion. It's not a purely isolation exercise, because it does involve the chest to some small degree, but I've found it works just as well.

They're easy to progress, too. At first they will likely be shaky, and you'll struggle to even get your elbows to the ground and back up. If you need to you can do them from your knees at first. But over time they'll smooth out, and work your triceps more and more as they do so. When you're doing them perfectly, dropping your elbows slowly and smoothly as you lower yourself, with your chest and elbows touching the ground simultaneously, they feel almost exactly like dumbbell triceps extensions.

From there you can elevate your feet and/or shift your weight forwards to put more load on the muscle. Or you could try getting it one-armed, if you're crazy! But I wouldn't try that. To me, isolation exercises are better done for high reps, and I don't think I'll ever get twenty perfect reps of these with my feet elevated and weight shifted forwards. They're pretty killer.
